gaps.sentence: The manager praised the team for its ___ (COMMIT) to quality.
gaps.explanation: The noun from COMMIT is 'commitment' — a dedication to a course of action.

gaps.hint: noun: the state of being free from rule
gaps.explanation: 'Gain independence' = become self-governing; the noun form follows the verb.

gaps.sentence: The factory will ___ (EMPLOY) fifty more workers next year.
gaps.explanation: The bare verb follows 'will': will employ.

gaps.sentence: There is no ___ (PROVE) that he was anywhere near the bank.
gaps.explanation: 'No proof that …' — the noun for evidence.

gaps.sentence: Do not be ___ (PATIENT) with the trainees — everyone learns at a different pace.
gaps.explanation: 'Do not be impatient' — the negative adjective fits the advice against frustration.

gaps.sentence: The company has made huge ___ (INVEST) in training.
He was praised for his ___ (BRAVE) during the fire.
gaps.explanation: 'His bravery' — quality noun; 'braveness' exists but is rare; 'bravery' is standard.

gaps.sentence: The new software ___ (ABLE) staff to work securely from anywhere.
gaps.explanation: 'Enable somebody to do something' — the present-tense verb fits the singular subject.
